$comment: THE BUDGET MECHANIC IS NOW KNOWN; ITS NUMBERS ARE NOT.
The 2K27 builder does not give you a pool of points to spend. It shows an OVERALL meter and the
instruction 'Fill to a 99 Overall to Continue'. You raise attributes, each raise moves your OVR,
and the build is finished when OVR reaches 99. (Screenshot: NBA 2K HQ app builder, 2026-08-26.)
So the real constraint is OVR(attributes) = 99 under the per-attribute caps, and the 'cost' of a
point in an attribute is that attribute's WEIGHT IN THE OVERALL FORMULA for your position. That is
a budget — a weighted-sum equality constraint — but it is not the one this file models.
WHAT THIS FILE STILL DOES: a flat point pool priced by cost-curves.json. It is the same SHAPE of
constraint (spend a scarce resource across attributes) which is why the optimizer's knapsack still
works, but the exchange rates are invented and the target is a made-up 2900 rather than 99 OVR.
TO FIX IT PROPERLY you need the per-position OVR weights. Nothing in the supplied sources publishes
them. Until then, treat every 'costs N points' figure in this app as ORDINAL, not cardinal: the
ranking of which upgrades are cheap is roughly right, the absolute numbers are not.
budget = base + perInchHeight*(h-ref) + perPoundWeight*(w-ref) + perInchWingspan*(ws-ref) + positionAdjust

verification.source: The 99-OVR mechanic is confirmed from the NBA 2K HQ app builder (2026-08-26); the point-pool model below is not.
verification.notes: The MECHANIC is sourced and is an OVR target, not a point pool. Every NUMBER in this file is invented, and the model is known to be the wrong shape.

notes: Body modifiers are all zero on purpose: in the NBA 2K series body settings move CAPS, not the
spending pool. They are exposed here anyway so you can model a budget effect if 2K27 has one.
`base` is calibrated against the invented cost curves in cost-curves.json so that a plausible
full build is exactly affordable. It is a joint fiction with those curves: changing one without
the other will make builds look either impossibly stacked or absurdly bare.
Both become obsolete the moment `actualMechanic.positionWeights` is filled in.

actualMechanic.$comment: Recorded so the shape of the real constraint is not lost, even though the engine cannot yet use it.

positionWeights.$comment: attribute id -> weight in the OVR formula, per position. Empty: not known. Fill this in and the optimizer can drop the invented point pool entirely.
